text: dsh-rea-toolkit 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 MCP 工具接入插件，通过配置将 REA stdio MCP 服务注册到 DSH，并提供本地软件分析工具。插件可启动随包提供的 REA runtime，也可在未配置本地路径时使用 npx 解析官方 runtime。适合需要在 DSH 中调用 REA 工具分析 JavaScript、Electron 应用及其他软件制品的开发者。启动方式由 DSH_REA_NODE 和 DSH_REA_HOME 环境变量决定；不需要 API key。首次配置可运行安装脚本准备 runtime，随后重启 DSH。

dsh-rea-toolkit connects REA to DSH as an stdio MCP service. The bundle starts a local REA runtime using DSH_REA_NODE and DSH_REA_HOME, or falls back to npx when unset. Developers can invoke REA analysis tools from DSH to inspect software artifacts. No API key is required.
想在 DSH 里通过 MCP 调用 REA 软件分析工具。
让 DSH 能启动本地 REA runtime 并分析 JavaScript 或 Electron 项目。
I want to use REA analysis tools from my DSH agent over MCP.
dsh-rea-toolkit 的功能「REA MCP 接入」：通过 DSH MCP 客户端以 stdio 启动 REA 服务。DSH 连接后可调用 REA 提供的分析工具，启动入口依据环境变量选择本地 runtime 或 npx 方式。
dsh-rea-toolkit 未配置本地 runtime 环境变量时会通过 npx 获取 rea-agents@6.7.0；该启动路径需要访问 npm registry。

dsh-rea-toolkit README · dsh-rea-toolkit：**One-line value:** after installing, your DeepSeek Harness agent gains the full [REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)](https://github.com/morluto/rea) toolset — evidence-backed static analysis of JavaScript/Electron applications, browser extensions, ASAR archives, .NET assemblies, native binaries, SQLite databases, WASM, EVM bytecode, and more — as native `mcp__rea__*` tools.

[](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/akash-digitavision/my-rea-toolkit)

dsh-rea-toolkit README · What it does：This bundle packages the **REA v6.7.0 runtime** (`dist/`, verified Windows native artifact, skills, and the exact dependency lockfile) together with a DeepSeek Harness **configuration-only MCP bundle** that registers REA's stdio MCP server through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`. REA analyzes targets **locally**; results include per-conclusion evidence and limitations.

Typical agent prompts after install:

dsh-rea-toolkit README · What it does：- *"Analyze the extracted extension at `D:/apps/legacy-ext` and list its modules, IPC channels and gateway endpoints with evidence."*
- *"Inspect this Electron app's ASAR and explain how the renderer talks to the main process."*

dsh-rea-toolkit README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:akash-digitavision/my-rea-toolkit
```

Then, inside the installed bundle directory, run the bootstrap **once** and restart DeepSeek Harness:

```sh
install-tools.bat      # Windows
./install-tools.sh     # Linux / macOS
node install-tools.mjs # directly
```

dsh-rea-toolkit README · Install：The bootstrap: discovers a suitable Node.js (22.19+/24.11+/26+), verifies the bundled REA runtime, installs REA's exact production dependencies from the shipped lockfile, persists `DSH_REA_HOME` / `DSH_REA_NODE` at user scope, and runs REA's own `mcp doctor`.

**Resolution contract** (see `cordis.patch.yml`):

dsh-rea-toolkit README · Install：| Environment | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `DSH_REA_NODE` + `DSH_REA_HOME` set | Absolute node + bundled, validated REA runtime (works with no system Node on PATH) |
| `DSH_REA_HOME` only | `node` from PATH + bundled runtime |
| Neither set | `npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 mcp` fetches the official runtime from npm |

Without any setup the bundle still installs safely — you simply get no REA tools until the bootstrap runs (or npm/npx is available).

dsh-rea-toolkit README · Compatibility：- DeepSeek Harness (DSH) with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` (shipped profile package).
- Windows 10+ x64 (uses the bundled verified `rea-windows-x64.node` Node-API addon; loader checks version/ABI/architecture/SHA-256 at load), Linux x64, macOS (Apple silicon: JS analysis lanes; native binary lanes per REA docs).
- Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ (auto-discovered by the bootstrap; the bundled DeepSeek Harness runtime qualifies).

dsh-rea-toolkit README · Permissions & external services：- **Local-only analysis:** REA reads the target files/directories you point it at and writes nothing outside its own analysis sessions. It does not upload targets anywhere.
- **Network:** only optional — npm registry (first bootstrap / npx fallback) and analysis targets that the agent explicitly asks to inspect over the network (e.g., a website URL via the browser lane).
- **Execution scope:** static analysis lanes do not run the analyzed application. Runtime capture lanes (browser observation, process capture, frida) run only when an agent workflow explicitly invokes them, with the harness user's permissions.
- **Ambient secrets** (`*TOKEN*`, `*KEY*`, …) are scrubbed from the MCP child environment by the Harness MCP client.

dsh-rea-toolkit README · License：- Wrapper (bundle, scripts, manifest): **MIT** — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
- Bundled REA runtime: **MIT** — see [runtime/rea/LICENSE](runtime/rea/LICENSE), [runtime/rea/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](runtime/rea/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [runtime/rea/DISCLAIMER.md](runtime/rea/DISCLAIMER.md). REA is for lawful analysis of software you own or are authorized to examine.
dsh-rea-toolkit README · Category：Development & Operations (secondary: Tools & Capabilities).

dsh-rea-toolkit README · Notes：- REA upstream: <https://github.com/morluto/rea> (not affiliated with this bundle).
- Native deep-analysis engines (Hopper / Ghidra / IDA) are bring-your-own and optional; JavaScript/extension analysis needs none of them.
- The `index.js` `apply(ctx)` export is an inert plugin-spec compliance shim; the bundle is configuration-only.
